right.desc: Divert resources to make more food.

left.desc: Ration what we have left.

right.desc: Cut down on power usage to other systems.

left.desc: We can't risk lowering our defences.

main_003.desc: NASA's lost VIPER rover rolls up to our airlock, flashing its headlights! Its link to Earth is dead, and its ice-scanner is pinging nearby.

right.desc: Charge it up and send it into a dark crater to hunt for water-ice!

left.desc: Park it on Shackleton Crater's sunny rim as a scout and solar charger.

main_004.desc: A shallow magnitude 4.5 moonquake is shaking the ground! The habitat domes are groaning as the fault line shifts underneath us.

right.desc: Power up the magnetic shock absorbers to steady the domes.

left.desc: Ride it out like the Apollo landers did and patch any cracks later.

main_005.desc: Our NASA 'Veggie' garden pods are drowning! In low gravity, water forms bubbles around the lettuce roots and stops them from breathing.

right.desc: Run air-circulation fans and UV grow lights around the clock.

left.desc: Harvest the soggy greens early and put the crew on freeze-dried rations.

main_006.desc: Glass-sharp moon dust is sticking to our spacesuits! It's chewing up the airlock seals and giving the crew 'Apollo hay fever.'

right.desc: Zap the suits with NASA's electric dust shield to shake the grit off.

left.desc: Have the crew brush each other off with wire brooms before coming inside.

main_007.desc: Our Kilopower nuclear reactor is running hot! We can push the uranium core harder for bonus energy, or cool it down to protect the shielding.

right.desc: Pull the control rod and push the heat engines to the limit!

left.desc: Throttle the reactor down and pile extra moon dirt over the radiation shield.

main_008.desc: A lunar satellite spotted a collapsed lava tube cave two kilometers away! Its thick stone roof offers natural protection from space radiation.

right.desc: Lower a tethered rover into the pit to haul up heavy volcanic rock for our walls.

left.desc: Too risky! Keep our drones near the base to tend the solar panels.

main_009.desc: The life-support water recycler is clogged! Low gravity makes the crew lose bone calcium, and that mineral buildup is jamming our urine filters.

right.desc: Use spare power to boil the filters clean and flush the pipes.

left.desc: Bypass the clogged filter! The water tastes metallic, but it saves power.

main_010.desc: Wait—is that Surveyor 3?! A scout found a 1960s NASA probe sitting in a crater, still wrapped in shiny foil and titanium struts.

right.desc: Do what Apollo 12 did: strip off its camera and metal tubing for spare parts!

left.desc: Turn it into a historical monument! Touring the site boosts crew morale.

main_011.desc: The Geminid meteor shower is pelting the Moon! With no atmosphere to burn them up, tiny space pebbles are hitting the surface faster than bullets.

right.desc: Raise the outer blast shutters and power up our impact shields!

left.desc: Leave the solar panels unfolded through the storm and patch any holes later.

main_012.desc: One of our cube-shaped NASA Astrobee robots went haywire in the cafeteria! Its little fans are blowing floating crumbs everywhere while it sings 'Daisy Bell.'

right.desc: Reboot its camera and put it back on air-leak patrol.

left.desc: Draw a smiley face on its screen and let the crew play low-gravity catch with it!

main_013.desc: NASA's Lunar Gateway space station is passing right overhead! They can drop us a spare supply pod if we guide it down to the landing pad.

right.desc: Fire up our high-powered laser beacon to guide the supply drop in safely!

left.desc: Let it crash-land in the soft dirt outside and salvage the crates on foot.

main_014.desc: Living in one-sixth gravity is weakening the crew's bones and making their vision blurry! Doctors warn that morale and health are slipping.

right.desc: Order 2 hours a day on NASA's vacuum workout machines to keep everyone fit.

left.desc: Skip gym time and put the crew on double shifts reinforcing the base walls.

main_015.desc: Our moon-dirt smelter is glowing at 1,600°C! Baking lunar soil separates out pure oxygen gas and leaves behind molten iron.

right.desc: Capture the fresh oxygen for the crew and store the leftover heat!

left.desc: Pour the melted iron into molds to make armor plates for our airlocks.

main_016.desc: NASA's deep-space laser dish just locked onto our receiver! We have ultra-fast internet from Earth for the next 20 minutes.

right.desc: Download solar-storm weather forecasts and power-grid software updates.

left.desc: Download movies, family video messages, and new recipes for the crew!

main_017.desc: Weird pink space-slime is growing inside our cooling pipes! Tough bacteria survived radiation and are now blocking water flow to the computers.

right.desc: Boil the pipes clean, then scoop out the dead slime to use as plant fertilizer!

left.desc: Vent the slimy water straight into space and refill from our emergency tanks.

main_018.desc: Our Valkyrie humanoid robot froze up while fixing the outer antenna! It's stuck hanging onto the tower as deadly shadow creeps in.

right.desc: Send a rescue team in a rover to haul Valkyrie back inside for repairs.

left.desc: Drain its battery pack through the power cable and leave the metal body behind.

main_019.desc: Our miners scooped up moon dirt packed with Helium-3 from billions of years of solar wind! The engineers want to test it in our experimental fusion generator.

right.desc: Fire up the Helium-3 reactor! Even a short burn will supercharge our batteries.

left.desc: Too dangerous! Sift the dirt for trapped nitrogen and hydrogen to feed our crops instead.

main_020.desc: We found an old Apollo laser mirror sitting out on the plains! Scientists on Earth still bounce green laser beams off it to measure the Moon's orbit.

right.desc: Send a scout with an air canister to blow the dust off the mirrors for Earth.

left.desc: Park a solar collector over the mirror to soak up the incoming laser energy!

main_021.desc: The crew in Habitat B has 'space cabin fever,' and the waste compactor is full! Weirdly enough, NASA research shows human waste is great at blocking radiation.

right.desc: Pack the sealed waste bags along the outer walls to block cosmic rays!

left.desc: Burn the waste in the plasma torch for steam power and throw a movie night!

main_022.desc: We dug up a pocket of 'Orange Soil'—tiny volcanic glass beads from 3.6 billion years ago, just like Apollo 17 found!

right.desc: Bake the beads at 900°C to cook out pure water and breathable oxygen!

left.desc: Melt the glass beads in our 3D printers to spin tough fiberglass dome armor!

main_023.desc: The two-week lunar night is at its coldest! It's -248°C outside, and the habitat's outer cooling pipes are about to freeze solid and burst.

right.desc: Divert warm air from the greenhouse lamps to keep the outer pipes thawed.

left.desc: Huddle everyone inside the warm reactor room and let the outer halls freeze!

alien_001_dip.desc: An alien delegation approaches the perimeter, broadcasting a peaceful mathematical sequence.

right.desc: Welcome them with open arms.

left.desc: Resources are low...

alien_001_com.desc: Alien vessels lock weapons onto our primary dome! Our refusal to share resources has provoked an attack.

right.desc: Defend ourselves!

left.desc: Sue for peace.

rover_001_ice.desc: VIPER's wheels are sinking into fluffy 'fairy-castle' moon dust inside a dark crater! Spinning the tires will only bury its belly deeper.

right.desc: Use VIPER's special suspension: lift and 'inchworm' each wheel out one by one.

left.desc: Fire the colony winches and drag it up the crater wall to the sunny ridge!

rover_001_scout.desc: The rover clipped a rock and ripped off its back fender! Now static-charged moon dust is coating its heat mirrors and cooking its electronics.

right.desc: Pull an Apollo 17 fix: clamp laminated colony maps over the wheel as a replacement fender!

left.desc: Drive it down into a freezing crater shadow to cool off before its circuits melt.

rover_002_ice.desc: At -235°C in the dark crater, VIPER's drill hits rock-hard ice! The drill is straining, and the rover's battery heaters only have 4 hours of juice left.

right.desc: Use NASA's 'bite-and-brush' method: pull the drill up every few inches to clear ice and warm the bit.

left.desc: Drop the stuck drill and sprint for a sunny ridge before the batteries freeze solid!

rover_002_scout.desc: Siren alert! NASA's space-weather satellites just spotted a huge Solar Flare heading our way. Radiation on the exposed ridge will fry the rover's computer!

right.desc: Trigger 'Safe Mode': park behind a giant boulder and shut down non-essential systems.

left.desc: Slide down the steep chute into the dark crater basin so the crater walls block the radiation!

rover_003_ice.desc: Jackpot! VIPER's scanners confirm the soil is 5% pure water-ice, plus trapped ammonia and carbon dioxide! It hauls a full load back to base.

right.desc: Melt the ice for our hydroponic farms and turn the ammonia into rich plant fertilizer!

left.desc: Split the water into breathable oxygen and rocket fuel to supercharge the colony!

rover_003_scout.desc: VIPER mapped a 'Peak of Eternal Light' bathed in 92% year-round sunshine, and found titanium-rich moon rocks along the ridge!

right.desc: Set up a tall solar tower on the peak and beam power straight to our colony grid!

left.desc: Bake the titanium-rich dirt into heavy radiation-shielding bricks for our domes.
